notes: Read SKILL.md in full (the only file). The skill shows how to serve ML models on Kubernetes with KServe and NVIDIA Triton: installing KServe via Helm, InferenceService manifests (sklearn and a GPU vLLM LLM), canary traffic splitting, KEDA autoscaling, a Triton Deployment and model repository layout, and model management commands.

Medium: following it has the agent run state-changing commands against the user's cluster with their kubeconfig: `helm repo add` + `helm install kserve` from kserve.github.io (SKILL.md:34-40), `kubectl apply`, and `kubectl patch` to shift or promote canary traffic (SKILL.md:160-167), plus curl calls that load/unload Triton models (SKILL.md:281-284). Acceptable because these are standard, user-requested deployment operations on the user's own serving cluster; there are no destroy/delete commands or security-control changes. A Hugging Face token is referenced only via a Kubernetes secretKeyRef (SKILL.md:123-127).

Review before adopting: the Helm install has no --version pin and images use :latest tags (SKILL.md:96, 133); GPU workloads are costly. Related Skills (SKILL.md:311-314) link to ../kubernetes-ops/ and ../../../infrastructure/{local-ai/vllm-server,local-ai/llm-inference-scaling,servers/gpu-server-management}/ as optional reading only.
